caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a donut chart illustrating the distribution of samples (%) across two measures of ambiguity: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity Std (Outer)," is divided into four segments corresponding to standard deviation values of 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94, represented by dark blue, medium blue, light blue, and very light blue, respectively. The percentages are 49.0% for Std: 0.0, 38.0% for Std: 0.47, 7.0% for Std: 0.82, and 5.0% for Std: 0.94. The inner ring, labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)," consists of three segments for maximum ambiguity values of 1, 2, and 3, shown in light blue, very light blue, and pale blue, respectively, with percentages of 39.0%, 47.7%, and 14.2%. Each segment in both rings is labeled with its corresponding percentage. A legend on the right side of the chart provides the color-coded mapping for both the outer and inner rings. The segments in the outer ring are ordered approximately by descending size, while the inner ring segments are arranged in ascending order of maximum ambiguity value.
